title: sanitized_environment removes the provider's own credential by name shape, and the authority record names two removals where three occurred
target: all declared targets; observed on gfx938
executor_revision: none: the run never reached a device

evidence.retained: two provider-qualification workspaces on bw1100, /home/testuser01/oci-dcu-runs/rmsnorm-20260917-152857 and rmsnorm-20260917-154028, each sealed at run task-provider-qualification with two events and protocol_adherence provider_fault
sites: src/open_cake_ir/lab/process.py:13-16 -- the name pattern, which matches AUTH and TOKEN as whole underscore-delimited components
src/open_cake_ir/lab/process.py:19-27 -- the projection applied to os.environ
src/open_cake_ir/lab/claude.py:777 -- the adapter hands that projection to the provider process
src/open_cake_ir/lab/claude.py:671 -- the same adapter writes removed_environment into the authority
rmsnorm-20260917-154028 provider_stdout object 68aafb3c -- apiKeySource none, and the assistant's only turn is 'Not logged in'

observation:
ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN matches the sensitive-name pattern twice, on _AUTH_ and on _TOKEN$, so the projection drops it. ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and ANTHROPIC_MODEL do not match and survive. Measured through the public function: with all three set, the projection returns the endpoint and the model and not the credential.

That pairing is the part worth stating plainly. The provider is handed an endpoint to talk to and a model name to ask for, and no way to authenticate to either. There is no environment in which that combination succeeds, so the harness cannot carry a credential through the environment at all -- not for this provider and not for any provider whose credential is spelled with one of six English words.

The incumbent host does not depend on it and so never showed it. B300-M2 carries the same endpoint, token and model in ~/.claude/settings.json under env, which the CLI applies to itself after the harness has sanitized what it inherited; nineteen campaigns there are evidence that the provider was reachable, not that the harness passed anything. A second host with no such file made the difference visible, and only three layers away: the removal happens in the Lab, the symptom is a login prompt inside the provider, and nothing between them says a name was dropped.

The record is wrong in the direction that matters. removed_environment is the authority's declared account of what this run removed, it names two, and a third was removed silently. A reader replaying that workspace cannot learn from it why the provider was not logged in. A removal decided by a regex and a removal decided by a list are one fact with two owners, and the owner that reaches the evidence knows about only one of them.
proposed_change: Two changes, and only the first is required for a run to work. (1) The credential a provider needs to reach its own endpoint is declared and forwarded by name, the way the endpoint and the model already are, rather than surviving or not surviving a pattern that was never about it; whatever the adapter forwards is what removed_environment accounts for, so the record is the whole truth. (2) Failing that, the pattern's removals are recorded alongside the explicit ones, so a sealed workspace states every name that was withheld. Do not widen the pattern to let one vendor's spelling through: that puts the provider's identity back in the else, and the next vendor spells its credential differently.
